questions.q: When should the acceptance criteria for an AI validation run be agreed?
options: After the run, based on the results
Before the run, with QA
At go-live
Only if the run fails
questions.why: Criteria set after seeing results are not credible evidence. Agree them with QA in the plan.

questions.q: Who should set the expected answers for the test cases?
options: The developer who wrote and tuned the prompt
The AI model itself, on a first run of the cases
Qualified people, or closed approved records
The vendor's sales team, who know the product best
questions.why: Expected outcomes must come from qualified people or approved records, not from the people building the tool.

questions.q: A prompt fix makes two failed cases pass. What do you rerun before approval?
options: The full protocol
Only the two failed cases
Nothing, the fix is small
A random three cases
questions.why: A fix can break other cases. Rerun the full protocol and compare with the last approved results.

questions.q: Under a risk-based approach, how should a low-risk formatting function be tested compared with a root cause suggestion?
options: Exactly the same way
Not at all
More deeply, since formatting is visible
Lighter testing if procedures allow it
questions.why: Effort follows risk. The root cause function needs scripted tests; low-risk formatting can be tested more lightly.

questions.q: Three months after go-live, reviewers start rejecting more AI drafts. What should already be in place?
options: A plan to switch the tool off on the first complaint
Monitoring thresholds that trigger an investigation
A brand new evaluation set built again from scratch
A note telling users to ignore the drafts for now
questions.why: Agreed thresholds on signals such as rejection rate should open an investigation, as for any GMP system.

questions.q: The model vendor announces it will retire the version you validated. What do you do?
options: Swap to the new version quietly over a weekend
Keep using the retired model through an unofficial route
Raise a change, rerun the protocol, get QA approval
Stop validating this tool, since the vendor changed it
questions.why: A model change is a configuration change. It goes through change control with the protocol rerun and QA approval.
